enum: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable / Can't tell: Retrospective qualitative documentary and arena-mapping case study complemented by 2 interviews rather than a longitudinal cohort; potential interview non-response or unavailable official records in Section 3.2 cannot be assessed because the provided text truncates after PDF page 74.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Not applicable / weak causal identification: Explicitly designed as an exploratory, descriptive, anti-positivist pragmatist qualitative case study (PDF pp. 25, 68-70, 73-74) reconstructing public arenas and controversies rather than estimating causal effects or controlling confounders.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Adequate in accessible framing, Can't tell for full empirical analysis: Chapters 1-2 accurately identify relevant federal, state, and municipal legal instruments—including Federal Law No. 12.334/2010 (National Dam Safety Policy), Federal Law No. 9.433/1997 (Water Law), Santa Catarina State Laws Nos. 6.739/1985, 9.022/1993, and 9.748/1994, Florianópolis Municipal Laws Nos. 239/2006 and 8080/2009, and Public Civil Action No. 5012843-56.2021.4.04.7200 creating the Judicial Chamber for Protection of Lagoa da Conceição (PDF pp. 17-23, 43-44)—but detailed empirical analysis of licensing, fines, and judicial proceedings in Chapter 4 is truncated after PDF page 74.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Can't tell: Institutional, participatory, and adaptive water governance dimensions are clearly defined in Chapter 2 (Quadro 5, PDF pp. 71-72), but the documentary coding rules, interview protocol, OBISF mapping procedures, and Iramuteq lexical analysis parameters in Sections 3.2-3.4 are truncated after PDF page 74.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak / secondary-source descriptive reporting in accessible pages (Chapter 4 truncated): Sanitation coverage (65.71% / 56%), disaster magnitude (130 million liters released, 75 residences invaded, 155 people affected, 3,000 tons of dead fish), and ecological degradation (dead-zone expansion, bathing-water quality controversies) are cited from secondary media reports, technical notes, and official statements (PDF pp. 7, 19-23), and Chapter 4 is not accessible in the truncated excerpt.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Can't tell: The literature review search and filtering (177 works) are transparently reported (PDF pp. 47-50), but empirical chapters (Sections 3.2-3.4 and Chapters 4-5, PDF pp. 75-291) are truncated in the provided full-text stream, preventing verification of completeness or selective quotation in empirical reporting.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Can't tell (with concern over tiny interview sample): Purposive selection of the January 25, 2021 Lagoa da Conceição CASAN effluent lagoon rupture case is clearly justified (PDF pp. 21-25), and actors were mapped via the OBISF platform alongside news and official documents, but primary interviewing was limited to only 2 local actors (PDF pp. 7, 25) and recruitment/corpus selection criteria in Section 3.2 are truncated after PDF page 74.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was there a clear statement of the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: The dissertation states an explicit guiding research question (PDF p. 25 / diss. p. 21), a clear general objective, and three aligned specific objectives (PDF p. 26 / diss. p. 22) focused on reconstructing the public arenas, controversies, and institutional/participatory/adaptive water (dis)governance processes surrounding the January 2021 Lagoa da Conceição dam/lagoon rupture, supported by detailed personal, academic, and societal justifications (PDF pp. 26-31).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 7 (Resumo); PDF Pages 25-31 (Sections 1.2, 1.3, 1.3.1, and 1.4, diss. pp. 21-27)

domain_ratings.justification: Qualitative inquiry is directly appropriate for reconstructing actor interactions, public arenas, competing narratives, vocabularies, and socio-technical controversies among public agencies, civil society, scientists, and affected residents following an environmental-sanitation disaster.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 7 (Resumo); PDF Pages 24-25 (Section 1.2, diss. pp. 20-21); PDF Page 73 (Section 3.1, diss. p. 69)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the research design appropriate to address the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: In Section 3.1, the author justifies an exploratory and descriptive qualitative single-case study design bounded around the Lagoa da Conceição CASAN effluent treatment lagoon/dam rupture, paired with pragmatist public-arena mapping and cartography of controversies to address the research aims.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 32 (Section 1.5, diss. p. 28); PDF Pages 73-74 (Section 3.1, diss. pp. 69-70)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the recruitment strategy appropriate to the aims of the research?
domain_ratings.justification: The Abstract and Introduction report that documentary research and OBISF arena mapping were complemented by only 2 interviews with involved local actors. Because the source text is truncated at PDF page 74 (before Section 3.2.2 Entrevistas, diss. p. 73), how and why those 2 interviewees were selected from a large multi-actor arena—and whether any invited actors refused—cannot be verified.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 7 (Resumo); PDF Page 15 (Sumário, Section 3.2.2); PDF Page 25 (Section 1.2, diss. p. 21); truncated after PDF Page 74

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the data collected in a way that addressed the research issue?
domain_ratings.justification: While the overview sections describe combining secondary news reports, official documents, OBISF platform mapping, and 2 interviews (and Section 2.4 details the October 17, 2022 academic literature search), the empirical data-collection protocols—documentary search/inclusion boundaries (Section 3.2.1), interview guide/recording procedures (Section 3.2.2), and OBISF mapping steps (Section 3.2.3)—lie past the PDF page 74 truncation cutoff and cannot be inspected.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 7 (Resumo); PDF Page 15 (Sumário, Section 3.2); PDF Page 32 (Section 1.5, diss. p. 28); truncated after PDF Page 74

domain_ratings.domain_name: Has the relationship between researcher and participants been adequately considered?
domain_ratings.justification: In Section 1.4.1 (PDF pp. 26-27), the author reflects on his Public Administration training, his 1 year and 9 months working in a municipal government, his NISP/OBISF affiliation, and how his own understandings evolved. However, whether he critically examined his positional relationship and potential influence vis-à-vis the two interviewees and local actors during empirical data collection and analysis cannot be verified because Sections 3.2.2 and 5.1 are truncated after PDF page 74.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 26-28 (Sections 1.4.1-1.4.2, diss. pp. 22-24); truncated after PDF Page 74

domain_ratings.domain_name: Have ethical issues been taken into consideration?
domain_ratings.justification: No information on research ethics committee (CEP) approval, informed consent (TCLE), or participant anonymity/confidentiality protections for the two interviewees appears in the accessible PDF pages 1-74, and Section 3.2.2 plus the Appendices are omitted due to truncation.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 1-74 (not mentioned in accessible pages; Section 3.2.2 and Appendices truncated after PDF Page 74)

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the data analysis sufficiently rigorous?
domain_ratings.justification: The Table of Contents, List of Figures, and Section 1.5 outline a multi-method qualitative analysis (OBISF network mapping, chronological case reconstruction, Iramuteq lexical/correspondence/similitude analysis of vocabularies, cartography of controversies, and theoretical triangulation). However, Sections 3.3-3.4 and Chapter 4 (diss. pp. 78-195) are truncated after PDF page 74, preventing direct evaluation of coding transparency, theme derivation, and handling of contradictory evidence.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 9-11 (Lista de Figuras/Quadros); PDF Page 15 (Sumário, Sections 3.3-3.4, Chapter 4); PDF Page 32 (Section 1.5, diss. p. 28); truncated after PDF Page 74

domain_ratings.domain_name: Is there a clear statement of findings?
domain_ratings.justification: Although the Abstract (PDF p. 7) summarizes the overarching argument regarding water (dis)governance across public arenas in Florianópolis, all empirical findings and conclusions (Chapters 4 and 5, diss. pp. 82-201) are missing from the truncated text after PDF page 74, so clarity, evidentiary support, and credibility checks cannot be verified directly.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 7 (Resumo); PDF Pages 15-16 (Sumário, Chapters 4-5); truncated after PDF Page 74

domain_ratings.justification: Valuable theoretical and contextual framing, though empirical value is only partially assessable due to truncation: Chapters 1-2 synthesize 177 Brazilian water-governance publications into a coherent tripartite framework (institutional, participatory, and adaptive governance) linked to pragmatist public-arena theory and address an under-studied urban sanitation disaster (the 2021 CASAN Lagoa da Conceição effluent lagoon rupture) connected to UN SDGs. However, empirical transferability and policy conclusions in Chapters 4-5 cannot be verified from the truncated excerpt.
domain_ratings.rating: Moderately valuable framing (empirical chapters truncated after PDF page 74)
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 23-31 (Section 1.4, diss. pp. 19-27); PDF Pages 47-73 (Sections 2.4-2.5, diss. pp. 43-69); truncated after PDF Page 74

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Ikeda (2024) is a Brazilian Master's dissertation in Public Administration conducting an exploratory, descriptive qualitative single-case study of water "(dis)governance" surrounding the January 25, 2021 rupture of CASAN's effluent treatment plant evaporation-infiltration lagoon/dam (LEI/ETE) in Lagoa da Conceição, Florianópolis. Appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist based on the accessible portion of the PDF (pages 1-74 of 291; truncated mid-sentence in Section 3.1), the dissertation clearly states its research question and objectives (Q1: Yes), appropriately adopts a qualitative approach to study multi-actor discourses and socio-technical controversies (Q2: Yes), and justifies its bounded qualitative case-study design and pragmatist theoretical synthesis of institutional, participatory, and adaptive water governance (Q3: Yes). However, 6 of 9 closed-response CASP items (Q4 recruitment strategy, Q5 data collection, Q6 researcher-participant reflexivity, Q7 ethical considerations, Q8 analytical rigor, and Q9 clarity of findings) must be rated "Can't tell" because Sections 3.2-3.4 and Chapters 4-5 (PDF pages 75-291) are truncated in the provided text, and the accessible summary indicates reliance on only 2 local-actor interviews alongside secondary news/documents and OBISF arena mapping. Legal and institutional frameworks (e.g., Federal Laws 9.433/1997 and 12.334/2010, state/municipal water and sanitation statutes, and Federal Public Civil Action No. 5012843-56.2021.4.04.7200) are accurately identified in the introductory chapters, while sanitation and environmental-disaster outcomes are cited descriptively from secondary sources.
raw_response.overall_rating: Moderate concern (6 Can't tell items; empirical methods §§3.2-3.4 and Chapters 4-5 truncated after PDF page 74 of 291)
raw_response.study_design_identified: Qualitative single-case study (exploratory and descriptive documentary research, OBISF public-arena mapping, cartography of controversies, lexical narrative analysis, and 2 interviews)
raw_response.where_found_summary: PDF Pages 1-74 of 291 accessible (truncated=true at diss. p. 70): Resumo/Abstract (PDF pp. 7-8), Lists of Figures/Tables/Abbreviations & Sumário (PDF pp. 9-16), Chapter 1 Introdução including objectives and researcher motivation (PDF pp. 17-33 / diss. pp. 13-29), Chapter 2 Discussão Teórica including 177-study literature review (PDF pp. 33-73 / diss. pp. 29-69), and Chapter 3 Metodologia Section 3.1 Desenho da pesquisa (PDF pp. 73-74 / diss. pp. 69-70). Sections 3.2-3.4 and Chapters 4-5 (PDF pp. 75-291) were truncated.
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The dissertation explicitly classifies its empirical design in the Abstract (PDF p. 7), Section 1.5 (PDF p. 32), and Section 3.1 (PDF p. 73) as an exploratory, descriptive qualitative single-case study ("abordagem qualitativa", "estudo de caso") combining documentary analysis of news and official records, public-arena and controversy mapping (OBISF), narrative vocabulary analysis, and 2 interviews with local actors. Under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, primary qualitative documentary/field case studies are appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist.
